summary.title: Machine Learning for Beginners: An Introduction to Neural Networks
summary.one_liner: You learn how neurons, feedforward passes, MSE loss, backpropagation and stochastic gradient descent fit together by building a small neural network from scratch in Python with NumPy.
keywords: how do neural networks work for beginners
train neural network to predict gender from height and weight
neural network without keras or pytorch
takeaways: A neuron multiplies inputs by weights, adds a bias, and passes the sum through an activation function such as sigmoid.
Feedforward means passing inputs through layers of neurons to produce an output.
Training means minimizing a loss such as mean squared error by adjusting weights and biases.
Backpropagation computes partial derivatives of the loss by working backwards through the network, and stochastic gradient descent uses them to update parameters one sample at a time.
The page includes a complete NumPy implementation of a 2-input, 2-hidden-neuron, 1-output network trained on a small height/weight dataset.
summary.summary: The post is a beginner-friendly introduction to neural networks that assumes no prior machine learning knowledge. It explains neurons, the sigmoid activation, and feedforward, then builds a small 2-2-1 network in NumPy. It covers mean squared error loss, backpropagation with partial derivatives, and stochastic gradient descent, using a toy height and weight dataset to predict gender. The page ends with a recap and links to further topics such as Keras, PyTorch, CNNs and RNNs.
